_note: HAND-CURATED coaching staff db - never overwritten by refresh. v2 schema (2026-08-03): hc/oc/dc blocks with since/playcaller/about, scheme knowledge deep-links into docs/knowledge chapters. Staff verified against 2026-dated sources 2026-08-03. dc may be null ONLY where the HC holds the defense with no DC title (currently TB). Edit freely; tests/unit/test_coaches_meta.py keeps this file complete.

hc.about: Younger brother of Matt LaFleur and a Kyle Shanahan protege (49ers, Jets OC, Rams OC 2024-25). Calls the offensive plays himself in his first head job.

oc.name: Nathaniel Hackett
oc.about: Ex-Broncos head coach and Packers OC under Matt LaFleur; hired the day of LaFleur's introduction to run install while the HC keeps the headset.

dc.name: Nick Rallis
dc.about: The NFL's youngest coordinator when hired at 29; retained as one of ten holdovers on the new staff, entering year four running Arizona's defense.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy play-action off wide zone; LaFleur calls it, Hackett installs

hc.about: Two-time AP Coach of the Year with Cleveland out of the Vikings/Kubiak wide-zone tradition; Atlanta's 20th head coach. A career play-caller deliberately handing the offense off here.

oc.name: Tommy Rees
oc.about: Former Notre Dame and Alabama OC who took over Cleveland's play-calling late in 2025; Stefanski says he's 'very comfortable' with Rees on the headset.

dc.name: Jeff Ulbrich
dc.about: Former Jets DC and interim HC, retained on a new three-year deal two days after Stefanski's hire; Atlanta's pass rush spiked in his first season.

offense_scheme.fact: Under-center wide zone, run-pass marriage, multiple personnel

defense_scheme.fact: Seattle/Rex Ryan hybrid with positionless versatility

hc.about: Fourth head coach in franchise history, from the Macdonald disguise-heavy branch: Michigan's 2023 national-title DC, then Chargers DC under Jim Harbaugh. Calls the defense himself.

oc.name: Declan Doyle
oc.about: The NFL's youngest play-caller at 29 - five years under Sean Payton, then Bears OC under Ben Johnson in 2025. Weaver calls him 'a human computer.'

dc.name: Anthony Weaver
dc.about: Ex-Dolphins DC in his third Baltimore stint; runs the defensive room and install while Minter owns the game-day calls.

offense_scheme.fact: Ben Johnson + Payton blend under Doyle

hc.about: Promoted from Bills OC after Sean McDermott's exit; Saints-raised under Payton and Carmichael, famous for LSU's 2019 passing game. Calls the offense, known for feeding the hot hand.

oc.name: Pete Carmichael Jr.
oc.about: Fifteen years as Saints OC and Brady's mentor from New Orleans; runs install and game-planning while Brady keeps the headset.

dc.name: Jim Leonhard
dc.about: Ex-Wisconsin DC and ten-year NFL safety from the Vance Joseph tree in Denver; converting Buffalo to a flexible attacking 3-4.

offense_scheme.fact: Under-center play-action, spread-the-targets philosophy

hc.about: Pete Carroll's longtime Seahawks assistant who revived Baker Mayfield as Bucs OC; announced at the 2026 Combine he's handing play-calling to Idzik to run the whole program.

oc.name: Brad Idzik
oc.about: 34-year-old who followed Canales from Seattle to Tampa to Carolina; 2026 is the first play-calling job of his career.

dc.name: Ejiro Evero
dc.about: Rams/Fangio-tree product and ex-Broncos DC; interviewed for three of the ten 2026 head-coaching openings before returning.

offense_scheme.fact: Condensed sets, Seattle lineage

hc.about: Turned Detroit into the league's best offense as Lions OC; the hottest offensive mind of his hiring cycle. Keeps the play sheet - motion, condensed formations, extreme 4th-down aggression.

oc.name: Press Taylor
oc.about: Promoted from passing-game coordinator; former Colts and Jaguars OC who runs install while Johnson calls the games.

dc.name: Dennis Allen
dc.about: Ex-Saints and Raiders head coach in his 30th year of coaching; overhauled the unit with 18 new defensive players.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy motion, RPO and gadget layers; Johnson calls it

hc.about: The AFC North's longest-tenured coach; McVay-tree Rams assistant who took Cincinnati to Super Bowl LVI and remains the offense's primary voice.

oc.name: Dan Pitcher
oc.about: Eleventh season on the staff and a rising 2027 head-coaching candidate; Taylor calls it 'collaborative' but kept the headset.

dc.name: Al Golden
dc.about: Former Temple and Miami head coach and Notre Dame DC; explicitly dialing up the blitz rate in 2026 after a historically low 17.6%.

offense_scheme.fact: 11-personnel spread; Taylor calls with Pitcher collaborating

hc.about: Architect of Georgia's back-to-back national-title offenses and Ravens OC 2023-25; first NFL head job and he keeps the play-calling.

oc.name: Travis Switzer
oc.about: Rose under Monken in Baltimore from quality control to run-game coordinator; Monken kept the headset citing Switzer's inexperience calling games.

dc.name: Mike Rutenberg
dc.about: Hired from Atlanta specifically to preserve the Schwartz system after Jim Schwartz resigned during Super Bowl week - Cleveland led the NFL in yards allowed over the prior three seasons.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy play-action off vertical concepts; Monken calls it

hc.about: Son of Marty and a 25-year OC journeyman who got his first head job at 51; run-game-first and intends to call plays as long as he's HC.

oc.name: Klayton Adams
oc.about: Former Cardinals OL coach who runs the ground game and weekly install; blocked from an Eagles OC interview and viewed as a 2027 HC candidate.

dc.name: Christian Parker
dc.about: First-time coordinator hired from Philadelphia, where he coached DBs under Vic Fangio; replaces the fired Matt Eberflus.

offense_scheme.fact: Condensed sets and play-action; Schottenheimer calls it

hc.about: Super Bowl XLIV winner across 15 Saints seasons and one of the era's defining offensive minds; gave up play-calling this offseason for the first time in his head-coaching career.

oc.name: Davis Webb
oc.about: 31-year-old former NFL quarterback promoted from pass-game coordinator when Joe Lombardi was fired; Payton cites how much 'quicker' Webb is, while retaining some calls.

dc.name: Vance Joseph
dc.about: Former Broncos head coach whose blitz-forward system produced new Bills DC Jim Leonhard; among the league's heaviest five-plus-man pressure rates.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy play-action; Webb now calls it

hc.about: Rebuilt Detroit into an NFC power on toughness and 4th-down aggression; took over play-calling mid-2025 after stripping it from John Morton, then handed it to Petzing as part of the 2026 hire.

oc.name: Drew Petzing
oc.about: Cardinals OC 2023-25 from the Stefanski/Kubiak lineage, hired in January after Arizona's staff change; Campbell relinquished the headset to him.

dc.name: Kelvin Sheppard
dc.about: Former NFL linebacker who rose from Lions LB coach; already drawing head-coaching buzz and adding coverage disguise studied from the top 2025 defenses.

offense_scheme.fact: Play-action heavy under Petzing

defense_scheme.fact: Moving toward more nickel and sub-package variety

hc.about: Shanahan-tree disciple with one of the best regular-season win rates of any active coach; runs the offense himself and has never given up the headset.

oc.name: Adam Stenavich
oc.about: Former OL coach who runs the ground game; drew Titans play-calling interest this offseason but stayed in Green Bay.

dc.name: Jonathan Gannon
dc.about: Cardinals head coach 2023-25 and the Eagles DC who reached Super Bowl LVII; replaced Jeff Hafley and is building the system around Green Bay's personnel.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy play-action, condensed splits; LaFleur calls it

hc.about: Franchise-icon linebacker turned 49ers DC and 2023 AP Coach of the Year; a Seattle/San Francisco single-gap disciple who increasingly delegates to run the whole operation.

oc.name: Nick Caley
oc.about: Ten years in New England then two with the Rams; retained for year two after Ryans and the GM publicly backed his in-season adaptability.

dc.name: Matt Burke
dc.about: Former Dolphins DC; across 2023-25 Houston allowed the second-fewest points per game (20.0) and forced the third-most takeaways.

offense_scheme.fact: Caley calls it

hc.about: Chargers OC then Eagles OC for the Super Bowl LVII run; a top-tier play-caller who builds around quarterback mobility and keeps the headset.

oc.name: Jim Bob Cooter
oc.about: Former Lions OC who drives weekly game-plan construction; drew an Eagles OC interview in January 2026.

dc.name: Lou Anarumo
dc.about: Six years as Bengals DC including the Super Bowl LVI run; known for game-plan-specific coverage menus rather than a fixed structure.

offense_scheme.fact: QB-movement elements; Steichen calls it

hc.about: McVay/LaFleur-tree riser ranked fifth in a 2026 poll of NFL play-callers, behind only Shanahan, McVay, Ben Johnson and Matt LaFleur. Calls his own plays.

oc.name: Grant Udinski
oc.about: 29-year-old from Minnesota's staff under Kevin O'Connell; assists Coen with in-game structure and situational work.

dc.name: Anthony Campanile
dc.about: His 2025 debut set Jaguars franchise records for rush yards allowed per game (85.6), takeaways (31) and interceptions (22) - and nearly the whole unit returns.

offense_scheme.fact: Condensed-formation play-action; Coen calls it

defense_scheme.fact: Varied fronts and pressure looks under Campanile

hc.about: Three-time Super Bowl champion and the winningest active coach; Holmgren/West Coast lineage and the source of a sprawling coaching tree. Still calls the plays.

oc.name: Eric Bieniemy
oc.about: Back for a second stint (2018-22 previously) after Commanders, UCLA and Bears stops; Reid keeps the headset.

dc.name: Steve Spagnuolo
dc.about: Three rings in Kansas City and three straight top-six scoring defenses; the league's premier exotic-pressure designer.

offense_scheme.fact: Spread-influenced, heavy motion, option routes; Reid calls it

KC.note: OC Eric Bieniemy on indefinite leave since late July 2026 (family emergency); duties split between Joe Bleymaier and Andy Heck.

hc.about: Won Super Bowl LVI and is the namesake of the sport's most prolific coaching tree; the youngest modern HC hire at 30 and still the primary play-caller a decade in.

oc.name: Nate Scheelhaase
oc.about: Former Illinois QB and Iowa State OC promoted internally after a second Browns HC interview; gets preseason play-calling reps alongside Dave Ragone.

dc.name: Chris Shula
dc.about: Grandson of Don Shula in his 10th season on the Rams staff; he and Scheelhaase were ranked the NFL's No. 2 coordinator duo entering 2026.

offense_scheme.fact: Condensed formations and play-action; McVay calls it

hc.about: Michigan national champion and 49ers Super Bowl coach with a run-first physical identity - and an excellent record of DC hires (Macdonald, Minter).

oc.name: Mike McDaniel
oc.about: Dolphins head coach 2022-25 and the most coveted offensive play-caller on the 2026 market; hired to modernize Justin Herbert's protection and passing game.

dc.name: Chris O'Leary
dc.about: 34-year-old from the Macdonald/Minter lineage - Chargers safeties coach in 2024, Western Michigan DC in 2025 - promoted to continue Minter's system rather than replace it.

offense_scheme.fact: Motion, condensed splits, speed-based play-action

hc.about: Son of Gary Kubiak and a Shanahan-system lifer - Vikings OC, Saints OC, then Seattle's play-caller for their 2025 Super Bowl team. First head job; calls his own plays.

oc.name: Andrew Janocko
oc.about: Kubiak's confidant since Minnesota and his QBs coach in New Orleans and Seattle; the calls are described as a staff operation.

dc.name: Rob Leonard
dc.about: Promoted from Raiders DL coach at 38; built his system from time under Mike Macdonald, Brian Flores and Steve Spagnuolo.

offense_scheme.fact: Under-center bootleg play-action; Kubiak calls it

hc.about: Former Boston College head coach who rebuilt his stock as Packers DC; a secondary specialist from the Ohio State/49ers zone-coverage world. Calls the defense himself in his first NFL head job.

oc.name: Bobby Slowik
oc.about: Kyle Shanahan's 49ers pass-game coordinator turned Texans OC, where he ran C.J. Stroud's OROY rookie year; promoted from senior passing-game coordinator in February.

dc.name: Sean Duggan
dc.about: Eight-year Hafley disciple across Ohio State, Boston College and Green Bay; runs the defensive room while Hafley owns game-day calls.

offense_scheme.fact: Outside-zone play-action under Slowik

hc.about: Sean McVay's Rams OC and a former NFL QB; 2024 Coach of the Year and the league's premier quarterback whisperer. Calls the offense himself.

oc.name: Wes Phillips
oc.about: Third-generation coach - son of Wade, grandson of Bum - who came with O'Connell from the Rams and runs install and game-planning.

dc.name: Brian Flores
dc.about: Former Dolphins HC whose creeper/simulated-pressure system is the most-copied blitz package in football; retained for a fourth season.

offense_scheme.fact: 11-personnel play-action; O'Connell calls it

hc.about: Three-time Super Bowl winner as a Patriots linebacker and 2021 Coach of the Year with Tennessee; took New England to Super Bowl LX in his first year back. Belichick-tree culture-and-toughness coach.

oc.name: Josh McDaniels
oc.about: In his third Patriots stint - 2026 is his 20th season in New England and 15th as OC; won 2025 AP Assistant Coach of the Year for Drake Maye's breakout, No. 2 scoring offense.

dc.name: Zak Kuhr
dc.about: Followed Vrabel from Tennessee and took over as interim in September 2025 when Terrell Williams was diagnosed with cancer, finishing top-four in points allowed; made permanent in February.

offense_scheme.fact: Matchup-driven, McDaniels calls it

defense_scheme.fact: Kuhr calls it; Williams now assistant HC

hc.about: Former Boise State/NFL QB who was OC for the Cowboys, Chargers and the Super Bowl LIX-winning Eagles before taking the Saints job. Calls his own plays.

oc.name: Doug Nussmeier
oc.about: Longtime college OC (Alabama, Michigan, Florida) who has worked with Moore at five stops since 2005; expanding tight-end usage in 2026.

dc.name: Brandon Staley
dc.about: Chargers HC 2021-23 and the Rams DC who broke through under the Fangio umbrella; his first Saints defense finished top-10 overall and 4th against the pass.

offense_scheme.fact: Vertical concepts with RPO layers; Moore calls it

defense_scheme.fact: Light boxes, heavy six-DB usage vs heavy personnel

hc.about: Won Super Bowl XLVII in 17 seasons with Baltimore before an offseason split; a special-teams-coordinator-turned-HC from the Andy Reid Philadelphia tree, hired to bring program-building stability.

oc.name: Matt Nagy
oc.about: 2018 Coach of the Year as Bears HC, then back in Kansas City as OC for two Super Bowl wins; an experienced play-caller brought in to develop Jaxson Dart.

dc.name: Dennard Wilson
dc.about: Titans DC the previous two seasons and Ravens DBs coach under Mike Macdonald in 2023; reunites with Harbaugh from Baltimore.

offense_scheme.fact: Heavy pre-snap window dressing under Nagy

defense_scheme.fact: Disguise and simulated pressures under Wilson

hc.about: Former Jets first-round corner and three-year Lions DC under Dan Campbell; survived an ugly 2025, made sweeping staff changes, and reclaimed defensive play-calling as his 'super power.'

oc.name: Frank Reich
oc.about: Former Colts and Panthers head coach and the Eagles OC for the 2017 title team; Stanford's interim HC in 2025 and a 1996 Jets teammate of Glenn.

dc.name: Brian Duker
dc.about: 36-year-old who worked three seasons under Glenn in Detroit before Miami's secondary; runs the room while Glenn takes the headset.

offense_scheme.fact: Under-center play-action under Reich

hc.about: Frank Reich/Colts-tree coach who has been to two Super Bowls and won LIX; more CEO and motivator than scheme architect - now on his sixth play-caller in six seasons.

oc.name: Sean Mannion
oc.about: 33-year-old former backup QB with one season as Packers QB coach and zero play-calling experience - the most aggressive upside bet of the 2026 cycle. Replaces the fired Kevin Patullo.

dc.name: Vic Fangio
dc.about: The namesake of the league's dominant modern defensive system and architect of the Super Bowl LIX defense; flanked by associate HC Clint Hurtt on the line.

offense_scheme.family: LaFleur/Shanahan wide zone + Eagles RPO core
offense_scheme.fact: QB-run game retained under Mannion

defense_scheme.fact: Light boxes, four-man rush - the original article

hc.about: The Steelers' 17th head coach, succeeding Mike Tomlin; Super Bowl XLV winner in Green Bay and ex-Cowboys HC, a classic West Coast teacher who calls his own plays.

oc.name: Brian Angelichio
oc.about: Came from Minnesota as passing-game coordinator under Kevin O'Connell and previously worked with McCarthy in Green Bay; the role is heavily shaped by how hands-on McCarthy is.

dc.name: Patrick Graham
dc.about: Four years as Raiders DC plus Giants and Dolphins coordinator stops; worked under McCarthy in Green Bay in 2018.

offense_scheme.fact: O'Connell play-action concepts layered in; McCarthy calls it

hc.about: Authored the NFL's No. 1 defense as Ravens DC before taking Seattle at 36; a Harbaugh-tree defensive mind who delegates the unit to Durde rather than calling it himself.

oc.name: Brian Fleury
oc.about: Seven seasons in San Francisco, most recently TEs coach/run-game coordinator; replaces Klint Kubiak and says he wants to 'maintain' what worked. First-time play-caller.

dc.name: Aden Durde
dc.about: London-born former practice-squad player turned Cowboys DL coach; Seattle finished top-five in defense in 2025 and he's a fast-rising HC candidate.

offense_scheme.fact: Fleury continuity from the Kubiak year

defense_scheme.fact: Disguise, sim pressures, heavy front variety

hc.about: Son of Mike Shanahan and the architect of the modern wide-zone/play-action system copied league-wide; two Super Bowl appearances. Recovering from a serious July 2026 car accident but expected for Week 1.

oc.name: Klay Kubiak
oc.about: Son of Gary and brother of Klint; fifth season on the staff, first as coordinator. Has handled practice play-calling for years and is doing so through Shanahan's recovery.

dc.name: Raheem Morris
dc.about: Falcons HC 2024-25 and the Rams DC for Super Bowl LVI; backed by heavyweight hires Matt Eberflus (assistant HC/defense) and Jerry Gray.

offense_scheme.fact: The original article - under-center play-action

SF.note: HC Kyle Shanahan limited in camp after a July 14, 2026 car accident (concussion, broken ribs/nose/hand); Chris Foerster running practices, expected back for Week 1.

hc.about: Jets HC 2015-18 and the Bucs DC who called the Super Bowl LV defense; a Parcells/Arians-tree defensive coach entering a do-or-die fifth season. Runs the defense personally - there is no DC on the staff.

oc.name: Zac Robinson
oc.about: Falcons OC for two seasons after rising through McVay's Rams staff; replaces Josh Grizzard, who left for Philadelphia.

offense_scheme.fact: Play-action and motion under Robinson

defense_scheme.fact: Amoeba fronts and fire-zone pressure - Bowles calls it himself; no DC title on the 2026 staff

hc.about: Jets head coach 2021-24, then 49ers DC in 2025; a Seattle-lineage defensive coach getting a second shot and reclaiming the defensive headset.

oc.name: Brian Daboll
oc.about: 2022 Coach of the Year as Giants HC and the Bills OC who developed Josh Allen; given essentially full autonomy to 'zig where the rest of the league zags.'

dc.name: Gus Bradley
dc.about: Former Jaguars HC and the original Legion of Boom coordinator whose system Saleh runs; publicly confirmed he will not call plays.

offense_scheme.fact: Deliberately gap-scheme and QB-run, not zone-based

hc.about: Won a Super Bowl as the Legion of Boom's DC and took Atlanta to Super Bowl LI; a culture-first leader who has vowed to let his new coordinator run the defense.

oc.name: David Blough
oc.about: Former NFL QB who last played in 2023, promoted straight from assistant QBs coach at 30 - one of the youngest play-callers in the league. Replaces the fired Kliff Kingsbury.

dc.name: Daronte Jones
dc.about: Longtime DBs coach and 2021 LSU DC arriving from Brian Flores' Minnesota staff; a first-time NFL coordinator replacing the fired Joe Whitt Jr.

offense_scheme.fact: Ben Johnson/Shanahan-influenced under Blough
